user: Audio export developers inspecting cue offsets and associated labels in a small WAV file.
pain: A cue marker can point beyond actual sample frames or refer to an address mode the export pipeline does not support.
capability: Map RIFF-WAVE chunk boundaries, resolve direct-data cue byte offsets and report orphan/duplicate/out-of-range marker references.
distinct: MIDI pedal, subtitles and media catalogs concern other event/metadata models. This inspects real binary WAVE sample/frame references and label linkage.
limits: Little-endian RIFF WAVE<=16MiB, exact declared file length, one fmt and one data chunk,16/18-byte conventional PCM or IEEE float fmt,<=64 channels; PCM8/16/24/32-bit or float32/64-bit. Validate block alignment,byte rate,frame divisibility,chunk boundaries/padding. <=5000 chunks per container,5000 cues and5000 labels. Resolve only cue data addresses with chunkStart=blockStart=0. Unknown chunks are opaque and listed; LIST/adtl labl is read. Text is shown as lossy UTF8 with original hex; CSET not interpreted. No playback, audio decoding, RF64/RIFX, wavl/playlist,extensible/compressed addressing, fact validation or full WAV validity claim. Unsupported cue addresses are findings, unsupported fmt is an error. Refuses example overwrite.
expected: The generated real eight-frame WAV resolves cue1 to frame3 and links its entry label.
checks: Actual stdlib wave oracle, byte offset resolution, duplicate/orphan/out-of-range addresses, odd chunks/padding, truncation, float and invalid format checks.
demand: Inferred workflow need; no verified request for this new product.
acceptance: The generated real eight-frame WAV resolves cue1 to frame3 and links its entry label.
